title: Noite Sangrenta
summary: A military rising in Lisbon on 19 October 1921 overthrew the government of António Granjo, and during the night that followed groups of armed men took Granjo, the former president Machado Santos and other republican figures from custody and murdered them. The killings were done in the name of a rising that had no plan for what came next, and no one was ever effectively punished for them. Historians treat the night as the point at which the First Republic lost the last of its credit with the officers and the middle class alike, and it is regularly cited among the causes of the acceptance that greeted the coup of 1926. It is in the atlas as the clearest single measure of how far the republic's politics had decayed.
